chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Marid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

saying: There is no believer who has a dairy goat in his home, except that the inhabitants of that home are sanctified and blessings are bestowed upon them. And if there were two, they are sanctified and blessings are bestowed upon them twice every day.

He said: Then one of our companions said, 'And how are they sanctified?' He said: An angel stands over them every morning and says to them: You are sanctified, and blessings be upon you, and you are made wholesome, and your food is made wholesome.
He said: I said to him, 'And what is the meaning of "you are sanctified"?' He said: You are purified (from sins).

key_terms.إِدَامُكُمْ: your condiment, sauce, or food accompaniment; what one eats with bread
key_terms.بُورِكَ: to be blessed; the passive form of bestowing divine blessing (barakah)
key_terms.طُهِّرْتُمْ: you are purified; specifically purified from sins and transgressions
key_terms.عَنْزٌ حَلُوبٌ: dairy she-goat; a she-goat that is milked regularly
key_terms.قُدِّسَ: to be sanctified; to be declared holy and pure

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the blessing of keeping a dairy goat at home?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that keeping a dairy goat in one's home brings sanctification and blessings upon the household. This teaching reflects the early Islamic agrarian context in which livestock, especially milk-producing animals, were valued both practically and spiritually. The Imam explains that an angel visits the household every morning to announce their sanctification and purification from sins, affirming a direct link between simple, wholesome living and divine blessing.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad Bin Marad who said, 
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying:

‘There is none from a Believer what happens to have a dairy goat in his home, except the inhabitants of that home are sanctified and Blessings are upon them. So if there were to be two, so they are sanctified and Blessings are upon them twice every day’.

So one of our companions said, ‘And how are they sanctified?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘An Angels pauses over them during every morning, so he is saying to them: ‘You are sanctified, and Blessings are upon you, and you are (made to be) good, and your sauce is (made to be) good’.
I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘And what is the meaning of ‘You are sanctified’?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You are purified (from sins)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Marid who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
If a family keeps a milking goat, reverence and blessing is sent on them. If they are two, the family is revered and blessed twice a day.’

Certain persons of our people then said, ‘How are they revered?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘An angels stands on them every morning and says, “You are revered and blessed, you are fine and your sauce is fine.’
I then asked, ‘What is the meaning of ‘ qudistum ’ (you are revered)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It means, ‘You are cleansed.’”
